paragraphs: The United Nations has a peace mission in south Lebanon. About 310 Irish soldiers work there now. The mission started in 1978.
The mission will end on 31 December. The United States did not want it to continue. After that, soldiers will have about two months to leave.
The European Union is planning a new, smaller mission. Its soldiers will train the Lebanese army. They will not keep the peace on the border.
Ireland has a rule called the triple lock. Because of it, Ireland can only send about 12 soldiers to the EU mission. The Government wants to change this law.
Some people are worried. They say Irish soldiers could be pulled into a war. Since 1978, 48 Irish soldiers have died in Lebanon.
sentZh: 聯合國在黎巴嫩南部有一個和平任務。
目前約有310名愛爾蘭士兵在那裡工作。
這個任務始於1978年。
任務將在12月31日結束。
美國不希望它繼續下去。
之後，士兵大約有兩個月的時間撤離。
歐盟正在規劃一個規模較小的新任務。
它的士兵將訓練黎巴嫩軍隊。
他們不會在邊境維持和平。
愛爾蘭有一項叫做「三重鎖」的規定。
因為這項規定，愛爾蘭只能派大約12名士兵參加歐盟任務。
政府想要修改這項法律。
有些人很擔心。
他們說愛爾蘭士兵可能會被捲入戰爭。
自1978年以來，已有48名愛爾蘭士兵在黎巴嫩喪生。

paragraphs: The United Nations peacekeeping mission in south Lebanon, known as UNIFIL, will end on 31 December after almost 50 years. About 8,000 soldiers serve in the mission, including 310 members of the Irish Defence Forces. The United States did not support a new mandate, so the mission must close. Troops will then have about two months to leave with their weapons and equipment.

In October, EU foreign ministers agreed to start a new EU mission in Lebanon. It will be much smaller, with about 160 people at first, and it will be based near Beirut. Its job is to train the Lebanese army, not to patrol the border.

At the moment, Ireland's triple lock rule means it can only send about a dozen soldiers to a mission without UN approval. Helen McEntee, the Minister for Defence, wants to change the law so that the Government and the Dáil can decide alone.

Some politicians are worried. Senator Tom Clonan said helping the Lebanese army could put Irish troops on one side of a possible civil war. However, a former head of the Defence Forces said the plan is just training, like an earlier EU mission in Mali. Over the years, 48 Irish soldiers have died in Lebanon.
